rule: receivers [--record] judges the recorded mainnet receiver set with gate.rules.judge in replay (an empty allowlist and the committed label store) and writes one fixtures/receivers/judgements/<subject>.json per subject of fixtures/receivers/set.json. The set is the last COUNTERPARTIES distinct counterparties of each account in RECEIVER_SOURCES (the FastNEAR Transfers API, newest first; implicit accounts are left out as the likeliest personal wallets, unless the label store holds them as a catalog token), then the NEAR accounts of intel/incidents/rhea.json, then the first CATALOG_SUBJECTS catalog_token NEAR accounts of the label store that are not in the set yet. A token subject is judged as the token of a transfer to TOKEN_RECEIVER, as intel/incidents/rhea.json judges its token contracts, and every other subject as the receiver of a NEAR transfer. --record chooses the set and fetches what is missing: the transfers pages, the view calls the rules make, and the NearBlocks keys and creation transaction for the first AGE_SUBJECTS receivers only (at most two NearBlocks calls each), so every later receiver without an earlier recording reads unknown on age. The view calls and NearBlocks answers live under fixtures/receivers/rpc/. Without --record nothing touches the network.
